subject: Post-demo: procurement path options & proposed MAP
summary: Post-demo qualification thread to confirm procurement route (PO vs card vs marketplace), identify procurement stakeholders, and agree on milestone timeline from legal -> security -> finance -> PO issuance. Agreed next steps: circulate MAP, provide sample redlines, and schedule procurement touchpoint.
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alaine Rojas <alaine@maplehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: procurement path options & proposed MAP

Thanks again for your time today, Alaine — great conversation and helpful context on compliance and billing needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with procurement expectations: 

Call highlights:
- Goal: pilot Redwood Inference (private VPC) on a small production workload starting Jan.
- Primary procurement constraints: (1) Legal wants a short review window for MSA redlines, (2) Security requires SOC2 evidence and an architecture diagram, (3) Finance needs vendor onboarding + PO issuance or marketplace billing clarity.

Procurement paths we discussed (please confirm preference):
1) PO (standard Redwood commercial MSA) — typical flow: legal review -> security questionnaire -> finance vendor setup -> PO issuance. Estimated 4–8 weeks depending on legal redlines.
2) Card (faster for low dollar pilots) — immediate onboarding, no vendor form required; limited to card-holder authority.
3) Marketplace (AWS Marketplace suggested) — can simplify billing but may require marketplace listing work and different MSA flow; may add ~2 weeks to contracting but reduces finance vendor setup.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — attached v1:
- Week 0 (this week): confirm procurement route (PO / card / marketplace) and identify procurement + security contacts.
- Week 1–2: legal receives MSA + any redlines; security team receives SOC2 + architecture diagram and completes initial questionnaire.
- Week 2–4: finance completes vendor form (if PO) and issues PO.
- Week 4: Redwood enables pilot environment and schedules kickoff.

Ask from you: please confirm who on your side is (a) legal lead for contract redlines, (b) security reviewer for SOC2/arch, and (c) finance contact for vendor setup or whether you prefer AWS Marketplace billing.

Attachments: Redwood_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf, MSA-redline-sample.docx

Happy to jump on a 30-min procurement alignment call this week if helpful — propose Wed 11/30 10am PT or Thu 12/1 9am PT.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement path options & proposed MAP

Thanks, Soojin — useful summary. A few quick notes from procurement side: 

- High level preference: PO if legal redlines are minimal. If the pilot budget is small (< $15k), finance may prefer card to accelerate.
- Legal: likely 2–3 reviewers; typical review window for an MSA with our vendor counsel is ~3 weeks, but that shortens if there are only minor redlines. I will confirm names by EOD.
- Security: SOC2 + architecture diagram are required. Security will run the vendor questionnaire; initial pass usually takes ~7 business days.
- Marketplace: we do use AWS Marketplace for some vendors, but for new product categories our procurement team asks for a Marketplace SKU + vendor relationship details — can be longer to set up.

Docs we need from Redwood: a clean MSA (we will send redlines back), SOC2 report (or letter), a network architecture diagram for the VPC deployment, and a completed vendor questionnaire.

I copied procurement (ctsproc) here — Carmen Lee (cced separately) will own the finance/vendor form. We can do your suggested slot Thu 12/1 9am PT to walk through the MAP and assign owners.

—Alaine
Alaine Rojas
Director of IT Procurement | Maple Health

Alaine — thanks for the clarity. A few pragmatic notes from similar accounts to set expectations: 

- PO route (typical): 4–6 weeks is common when legal redlines are minor and security responses are provided in week 1. If legal engages external counsel, plan 6+ weeks.
- Card route: can be same-day to 1 week depending on internal approvals; good for pilot <$15k as Alaine said.
- Marketplace: reduces finance vendor setup but can add ~10 business days for SKU/onboarding depending on listing status.

I attached: vendor-questionnaire-answers.xlsx (pre-filled where we can) and MSA-redline-sample.docx (callout notes on the common redlines we accept). That should speed review.

If you confirm PO route, typical milestone timeline we commit to in MAP: legal to redline within 10 business days, security turnaround 7 business days after receiving our SOC2 + diagram, finance issues PO within 5 business days of completed vendor form.

Looking forward to Thu 12/1 9am PT. I'll prepare the call slide with timeline milestones and a short checklist of items to get into Carmen's hands immediately.

Best,
Ben Carter
